Script:


KRUGERSDORP KILLERS 3


V/O: The ongoing trial of the Krugersdorp Killers has heard ludicrous testimony of witches, vampires and werewolves. But precious lives were lost. These are the eleven victims who were brutally murdered between 2012 and 2016. Neither friends, family, nor acquaintances were safe when the group Electus Per Deus went on a senseless killing spree motivated by revenge and greed.

High school teacher Marinda Steyn, her son Leroux Steyn and friend, John Barnard, have pleaded guilty and been sentenced. Her daughter Marcel Steyn, friend Zak Valentine and alleged mastermind Cecilia Steyn have pleaded not guilty and deny any knowledge of the crimes.

Link: This complex and bizarre trial has been in court for 7 weeks. The State called 52 witnesses; both Zak and Cecilia have given evidence. The defense has only called one witness – Marinda Steyn – and her testimony was chilling.

Andre: Leroux testified that Accused 2, Cecilia, got upset with Pastor Reg Bendixen. Do you know anything about that?

Marinda: It’s not true, I got upset with him because he changed Ria. So, I went to Zak and I said to him I want to kill this man.

V/O: Posing as police officers Marinda & Zak entered Bendixen’s property on the 13th of August 2012.

Marinda: I was busy talking to him when I saw that Zak was ready behind, he had an axe, he was going to hit him with the blunt side of the axe over his head, so I could stab him. Because I wanted to stab him. I showed Zak yes. Then he hit him over his head and when he was down Zak kept on hitting him. I told him I want to kill this man, so I told him to stop and he was still hitting when I started stabbing Reg. He couldn’t stop himself hitting him, he nearly hit my head. I lifted his jersey and I stabbed him until I thought he must be dead and then I remembered you have to see if the blood is still running, so I stabbed him in the throat here to see if it’s still pulsing, and I watched it until it stopped, and then we left.

Andre: Did you at any stage tell Accused 2 what happened?

Marinda: No! no, no that was something I had to keep away from everyone else then. I started living a life separate from being a teacher and a mother and a friend.

V/O: But the State alleges that Accused 2, Cecilia Steyn, is the master-mind, who manipulated the group into believing they were doing good and fighting evil.

John: I took a loan out at the bank, at Capitec for R50 000, and that R35 000 was part of it.

Gerrie: Why did you transfer that large amount to Cecilia?

John: Because she said she needed the money for an orphanage. She used to be a full-on satanistic person and all Satanists what they do is, they actually giver their first born up for a ritual for the devil. And she says some people do not want to do that, some of the parents, and what they do is, they give their first born away to her and she is looking after these children and so on at the private orphanage.

Zak: Cecilia told us that there is people that is coming out of the Satanic church, witches that wanted to hide away from the Satanic church and that we needed to send them overseas to be protected. So I did everything I could financially for the gain of the Kingdom of Christianity.

Amanda: So whatever financial assistance you were giving would be handed to Accused 2?

Zak: That is correct. On a monthly basis I would say between R50 and R70 000. Over the whole incident I would say far over R2 million.

Ros: I can see him being easily influenced. He’s the kind of person who would actually be a follower and not a leader. There’s this psychopathology; he was greedy.

V/O: Psychologist Rosalind MacNab attended the trial and listened to the testimony of the group.

Ros: What is very, very evident is that in all of these characters there is no remorse, no empathy.

Devi: Do you believe that Cecilia was the centre of all of this, that she was the mastermind?

Ros: I totally believe it. Cecilia formed this cult. As a cult leader she fits all the descriptions.

V/O: We delved into Cecilia’s background, and went to visit her parents. Piet and Mara Brand live on plot in Randfontein and haven’t seen their daughter for almost two years.

Piet: She was a problem child. She was expelled from Westonaria High School over the same things. She’s a big talker, scares other children with her talk. There were never any Satanists, but if you’re a Satanist then she’s a bigger one; if you’re an alcoholic, then she’s a bigger one; if you’re a lesbian then she’s a bigger lesbian – but she is a lesbian. Her Mother always covered it up and hid it away. She hid it away, hid it away, where is my child today? Jail. I am very heartsore, because I love her very much!

Devi: Mara, what was Cecilia like as a child?

Mara: Yes, you know she was always the centre of attention when they played. She always played a leadership role. She was the leader of the pack.

Devi: When did she go away to boarding school?

Mara: Her sister was in Petrus Steyn in the High School, so she also wanted to go to Petrus Steyn. So in Grade 2 I put her in Petrus Steyn. She was six.

Piet: I wanted to go and attack the housemaster in Petrus Steyn, because she was in the hostel there. He phoned me and told me my child smashed a window at the bottle store and stole a bottle of booze. I called him a liar, but today I know she did do it.

Ros: This is what we would call a conduct disordered child who grew up to actually be an anti-social personality - not a-social - but meaning a psychopath.

Link: Several witnesses have testified about Cecilia’s different alter-egos that co-exist with her own. They have different names and ages; she claims to have been diagnosed with DID, Dissociative Identity Disorder.
Gerrie: Can you name some of those personalities?
Candice: There were countless. There was Xena, there was Lilith, there was Lilly, there was Akisha. The list literally goes on. There was a good couple 100 different parts anywhere ranging from babies that needed to drink bottles to DID parts her age.

Gerrie: Is it correct that DID kicks in as a child, when you have early trauma at an early age in your life?

Cecilia: They say so, yes.

Gerrie: What was the trauma at the early stages of your life?

Cecilia: I couldn’t be able to answer that.

Gerrie: Why not?

Cecilia: Because I was seeing a psychologist and we were doing hypnosis about it.

Gerrie: Are you saying you don’t know, are you don’t want to answer?

Cecilia: I’m saying I do know but I’m also saying I don’t want to answer.
I didn’t grow up in a pretty much perfect house, so obviously there was trauma, it caused DID, what more can I tell you?

Gerrie: What kind of trauma?

Cecilia: Physical abuse trauma.

Gerrie: Assault?

Cecilia: Amongst other things, yes.

Gerrie: What are the other things?

Cecilia: There are lots of different ways to traumatize a child. So as a child you cannot physically run away, you can’t. So what runs? Your mind runs, because it’s the only thing that can escape is your mind, and that’s how DID starts. It’s a God-given ability to survive.

Devi: When she was growing up, Cecilia, was she ever exposed to any traumatic event?

Mara: No.

Devi: Was she physically abused?

Mara: No, my husband never hit her. I once gave her a terrible hiding that the school called me to say I can’t hit a child like that.

Amanda: Did you have a happy childhood?

Cecilia: Happy as can be, yes.

Amanda: There was no instances of sexual abuse?

Cecilia: No.

Amanda: Not at all?

Cecilia: I would not say abuse not at all, but not sexual abuse, no.

Amanda: Molestation?

Cecilia: No.

Amanda: You do agree that you suffer from DID?

Cecilia: Yes, I do.

Ros: None of her personalities or her alter egos ever showed themselves in Court.

Devi? What does that say?

Ros: I think that indicates that she could be quite a good little actress.

Devi: What sort of person malingers, or pretends to be sick?

Ros: A very good liar, and she is a pathological liar.

Devi: Do you believe Cecilia was involved in all those murders?

Piet: No. I believe she is sitting there because of her big mouth. She is a big talker, but she is not capable of murder.

V/O: Unlike Zak who, according to Marinda’s testimony, allegedly killed 6 of the victims himself.

Link: Zak Valentine denies any involvement with the murders, but the one charge he can’t distance himself from is the killing of Jarod Jackson and the faking of his own death.

V/O: On the 16th of December 2015 Jarod Jackson was drugged and strangled, before being placed in Zak’s Mercedes Benz which was set alight near Petrus Steyn. The group then claimed R3.5 million on Zak’s life insurance policy for his beneficiary, Cecilia Steyn. But Zak’s version of events is utterly absurd.

Zak: Before I left everything Accused 2 also gave me some juice. The last time which I could remember was Vanderbijlpark, when I drove through Vanderbijlpark, and I remember totally losing consciousness. And what I could remember after that, is I was in a BMW, my 330d, and we were just outside Krugersdorp.

V/O: He claims Marinda then walked him into the Herberg Hotel and told him to lay low.

Gerrie: What is your take on that version?

Marinda: It’s a far-fetched lie.

V/O: Zak pretended to be dead for another 6 months, claiming he’d received threatening SMS’s from the Satanic church.

James: He would need to place evidence before the court to raise a reasonable possibility of this fact. But until he does so, it’s not really going to fly.

V/O: Advocate James Grant believes the group was acting in concert together.

Devi: Cecilia wasn’t present at any of the murders, and she claims not to have known about any of them. But when we start talking about common purpose, things start getting a bit slippery?

James: If you entered into a common purpose with those who did do the deed, then it doesn’t matter if you are sitting at home, or down or in Cape Town when the murder occurs up in Johannesburg. The law takes the view that you were both in Cape Town and up here, and if it was, as in some of the cases, a strangulation, then you were in Cape Town and busy strangling somebody at the relevant time. So it’s all about common purpose, where you were is irrelevant.

V/O: Accused 3 Marcel Steyn is expected to take the stand when the trial resumes in May 2019.
